description: Failure-first operational health, bounded reliability signals, logical-interface drill-downs, announce flow, request traces, and structured events for prnsd.

panels.description: Liveness only: LIVE means the daemon published a runtime snapshot within two minutes.
panels.title: Daemon live

panels.description: HEALTHY: nothing wrong in the last 5 minutes. DEGRADED: routes got evicted or a table ran out of room. FAULT: the runtime hit a hard failure. Egress lane shed is normal backpressure and does not affect this. Interface up/down and host problems are shown separately and do not affect it either.

targets.expr: 3 * ((max(last_over_time(prns_runtime_up[2m])) or vector(0)) == bool 0) + ((max(last_over_time(prns_runtime_up[2m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0) * clamp_max(2 * (((sum(increase(prns_egress_frames_total{outcome="lane_missing"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_announces_egress_total{outcome=~"ifac_rejected|pacer_rejected"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_announces_ingress_total{outcome=~"held_dropped_.*"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_operations_total{outcome!="succeeded"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_resources_failures_total{cause!="cancelled_by_sender"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_links_closures_total{reason=~"timeout|malformed_rtt"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_links_interface_mismatches_total[5m])) or vector(0))) > bool 0) + ((((sum(increase(prns_routes_removals_total{cause="evicted"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0) + ((sum(increase(prns_engine_ignored_packets_total{reason="capacity_exhausted"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0)) > bool 0), 2)

panels.title: Operational state

panels.description: Actionable failure signals in the last five minutes. Related counters can describe the same incident, so this is a signal count rather than a unique-incident count.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(prns_egress_frames_total{outcome="lane_missing"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_announces_egress_total{outcome=~"ifac_rejected|pacer_rejected"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_announces_ingress_total{outcome=~"held_dropped_.*"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_operations_total{outcome!="succeeded"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_resources_failures_total{cause!="cancelled_by_sender"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_links_closures_total{reason=~"timeout|malformed_rtt"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_links_interface_mismatches_total[5m])) or vector(0)))

panels.title: Hard signals · 5m

panels.description: How many pressure signals fired in the last 5 minutes: route eviction and table capacity. Egress lane shed does not count here, it is normal backpressure. Interface up/down and crypto work deferrals do not count either.

targets.expr: (((sum(increase(prns_routes_removals_total{cause="evicted"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0) + ((sum(increase(prns_engine_ignored_packets_total{reason="capacity_exhausted"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0))

panels.title: Degraded conditions

panels.description: Persistence, identity, configuration, interface-start, and shared-instance failures from structured daemon events.
panels.title: Host faults · 5m

panels.description: Connected or degraded interfaces are online.

panels.title: Hard failure breakdown · 5m

panels.description: Counts from the last 5 minutes: routes evicted, packets dropped because a table was full, and frames shed because a send queue was full. Lane shed is blue because it is normal backpressure: peers resend and recover, and it does not make the runtime count as degraded.
panels.title: Bounded-capacity pressure · 5m

panels.description: Every logical interface not currently Connected, by name and exact state. This is informational and does not lower Operational state.

panels.title: Interface attention

panels.description: Settled caller-visible failures by bounded operation and exact outcome.
panels.title: Operation failures

panels.description: Incoming resource failures and abnormal link closure or interface-mismatch signals. Peer-requested closures and sender cancellations are excluded here.
panels.title: Resource and link failures

panels.description: Malformed, invalid, refused, rate-limited, and capacity-exhausted ingress. Routine duplicate, superseded, not-for-us, and loop-prevention outcomes are intentionally excluded.
panels.title: Rejected ingress and capacity

panels.description: Total data sent and received since the daemon started. Same numbers as prnsd status --totals.
panels.title: Traffic since up

panels.description: Current engine and interface-pacer pressure. Stable zeros are healthy.
panels.title: Announce pressure

panels.description: How fast the whole node is sending and receiving. Computed from the byte counters, so short bursts always show up.
panels.title: Node traffic

panels.description: How long requests take, from tracing spans. prns.respond is a request this node answered, and every one is recorded. prns.request is a request this node sent out itself, and only 1 in 10 is recorded. Tempo can only compute this over a window of 3 hours or less.
panels.title: Outbound Request Latency

panels.description: How many requests this node answered (like a page fetch from its hosted pages) and how many it sent out itself, per time slice, split by outcome.
panels.title: Inbound Requests

panels.description: Frames skipped because their interface was not online. This is not packet loss and does not lower Operational state; sustained activity identifies where connectivity is absent.
panels.title: Unavailable egress

panels.description: Packets and host commands ingested by the engine, and frames enqueued for egress.
panels.title: Engine throughput

panels.description: Saturation of the offloaded cryptographic worker pool. Sustained depth near the high-water mark or a growing verdict debt means inbound packets are waiting on cryptographic work.
panels.title: Cryptographic queue

panels.description: Cryptographic jobs submitted and completed, with backpressure deferrals when the pool refuses new work.
panels.title: Cryptographic jobs

panels.description: One bounded row per logical interface, including whether it was configured or discovered. Fleet peers roll up beneath their TCP, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, backbone, WebSocket, or shared-instance supervisor.
panels.title: Interface overview

panels.description: How much data each interface moved in the selected time range. Relayed traffic counts as received on one interface and transmitted on another.
panels.title: Busiest interfaces · selected range

panels.description: How fast each selected interface is sending and receiving. Computed from the byte counters, so short bursts always show up.
panels.title: Interface traffic

panels.description: Validated ingress outcomes and egress outcomes for the selected logical interfaces.
panels.title: Interface announce flow

panels.description: Announce queues that currently have something waiting in them. Empty panel means nothing is queued anywhere, which is the normal state.
panels.title: Interface announce pressure

panels.description: How much data moved in each time slice, one color per interface. Received is above the line, transmitted below. Relayed traffic shows a bar above and a matching bar below at the same moment: that pair implies the likely the path it took. Hover to see the names. Always shows all interfaces, ignoring the filter. Slices are 1 minute zoomed in, wider zoomed out.
panels.title: Relay flow · all interfaces

panels.description: Which interfaces are carrying relayed links right now. A relayed conversation counts on both the interface it comes in on and the one it goes out on, so matching lines are a pair.
panels.title: Transit links by interface

panels.description: Validated announces as they enter the engine, including held and capacity outcomes.
panels.title: Inbound announces

panels.description: Announce frames accepted by outbound interface lanes after any applicable pacing and IFAC masking.
panels.title: Outbound announces

panels.description: Pacer rejections, IFAC failures, and missing or full lanes split by announce origin.
panels.title: Announce egress failures

panels.description: Prns-owned announce command outcomes. Shared-client and relay traffic is shown in the outbound panel.
panels.title: Local announce commands

panels.description: Accepted inbound announces grouped by their receiving interface kind.
panels.title: Inbound announce interfaces

panels.description: Announce frames accepted by each outbound interface kind.
panels.title: Outbound announce interfaces

panels.description: Warnings and errors retain their structured event names and diagnostic fields.
panels.title: Warnings and errors

panels.description: Searchable structured lifecycle and diagnostic events from prnsd stderr.
panels.title: Recent prnsd events
